title: test: real newsreader client interop (slrn, tin, Thunderbird)
description:
CLAUDE.md requires RFC 3977 conformance tests to be driven by real unmodified newsreader clients against a live reader process, not mocked. Current conformance tests use Python nntplib (integration-tests/tests/nntp_conformance.rs), which is a good programmatic check but does not catch client-specific quirks, pipelining assumptions, or capability negotiation edge cases that slrn/tin/Thunderbird exhibit in practice.

Why this matters: the reader must work with standard newsreader clients without modification. Library-level tests cannot substitute for actual client smoke tests.

What needs to be done:
1. Add a docker-compose service (or justfile target) that runs a live stoa-reader instance with test data pre-seeded.
2. Drive slrn in batch/script mode against it: CAPABILITIES, GROUP, ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY, OVER, AUTHINFO, STARTTLS round-trip.
3. Drive tin in similar batch mode.
4. Drive Thunderbird via its CLI (thunderbird --headless or a profile automation script) to verify folder listing, article fetch, and post.
5. All three must complete without errors or unexpected responses.
6. Add the tests to CI as an optional integration step (requires Docker).
